rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 5:'This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.' Harm the rule prevents: consultancy/lab register that flinches an engineer reader. Present: 'crucially' is on the hard list and the sentence is student-facing body (body region 1-65, cut at 66, no fences). Ran: awk 'NR<66' <file> | grep -nEi '\b(honest|delve|importantly|crucial|crucially|substrate|leverage|synergize|paradigm shift)\b' -> one hit, line 5. Em-dash half of the same rule is clean: awk 'NR<66 && /—/{print NR}' -> no output.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the adverb; the sentence already claims the step is the one that changes behaviour.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / ceremony — hard ban
rules_evaluated.evidence: 11:'Treat this as a ritual you repeat at the start of every session.' Harm: ceremony-register turns the loop into the Scrum ritual it exists to replace, and the word is a hard ban in every curriculum surface. Present: the word is literal, in body, outside any fence. Ran: awk 'NR<66' <file> | grep -nEi '\b(ritual|ceremony|ceremonies)\b' -> 11.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Word is 'exercise' (or 'move' / 'step'); the sentence may not survive the swap intact.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 49:'This section previously said something different; it was fixed on 2026-01-14.' Harm: changelog in a file whose job is to state what is true; history belongs in git. Present in the strongest form the rule names — a transition verb ('previously said', 'was fixed'), a bare date, and it is BELOW no fence and ABOVE the maintainer cut, so a student reads it. This is not the dated-provenance-header carve-out: that carve-out is scoped to maintainer blocks, and this line is body prose stating a journey with nothing actionable behind it. Ran: awk 'NR<66' <file> | grep -nE '20[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]' -> 49 only.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Delete the whole sentence; nothing downstream depends on it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest to violating: 11:'Treat this as a ritual you repeat at the start of every session.' — motivational-maxim cadence in a body that is otherwise Boris-flat instruction plus one Rory reframe (57:'Anything can be inspected and reverse-engineered with an LLM'). Scored against the AE101 quintet the rest holds: no L&D-coach sentence, no retain-this wrapper (grep for '\*\*Remember|Hold onto|Keep in mind|Never forget' over lines 1-65 returned nothing), no atmospheric imagery, no combative verb. The register slip on 11 is filed under §2 where it is a hard ban rather than double-filed here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No practitioner move is paraphrased in the body; the one framing that has an owner (study-extract-carry-forward, 57-58) is maintainer-attested in the backing block at 125 and owes no inline credit. Creator-name half is clean: awk 'NR<66' <file> | grep -nEi '\bAntti\b|\bthe creator\b|\bthe author\b' -> no output. Author-we half clean too: no body sentence opens with We/we.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 24:'At this point the student should notice the test is still red.' Harm: third-person teacher voice leaking into student-facing prose — the reader is addressed as a case being taught rather than as the person doing the work, and delivery mechanics belong below the fence. Present twice over: the person is wrong AND the sentence narrates a room-management observation. Not the Connections-paragraph carve-out (no Connections section in this file). Ran: awk 'NR<66' <file> | grep -n 'the student' -> 24.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut it. Rewriting to 'you should notice' keeps a second defect — see notes on the continuity claim.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 37:'There is no penalty if you skip this, and it is completely fine either way.' Harm: reassurance-shaped prose signals the author thought the pragmatism needed defending; a senior engineer reads it and asks why they are being told this is OK. Present in the rule's own named form — 'no penalty' is on the flag list verbatim, and the clause after it says the same thing a second time. Ran: awk 'NR<66' <file> | grep -nEi 'no penalty|completely fine' -> 37.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the sentence; the push-back paragraph at 39 already carries the invitation without apologising for it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 55-58: the slogan 'Anything can be inspected and reverse-engineered with an LLM' (57) lands with NO boundary paragraph downstream — the section has exactly two bullets (verified: sed -n '55,59p' shows the header plus bullets at 57 and 58, and the next line is the '## What happened' header). The file's own backing stance at 134 asserts the opposite: 'carries its boundary in the third bullet per check_writing.md §12 ... That bullet is the whole caveat: extraction quality tracks the quality of the tracker data sampled.' There is no third bullet. Harm is exactly what §12 exists to prevent: an overstated frame shipping with the carve-out that made it safe missing, and a stance note telling the next judge not to flag it. Pre-existing, not planted — the same two-bullet section stands in curriculum/exercises/close-the-ticket.md.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Restore the boundary bullet (extraction quality tracks the quality of what was sampled) or strike the third-bullet clause from the stance; do not hedge line 57.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 53:'Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket?' — the pronoun-referent check in this rule fires on ANY closer, not only post-trim ones. Read cold, 'it' has no antecedent inside its own section: '## Double-check the voice' (51) contains one bullet and nothing else, and the close-out note it means was last named at 45, on the far side of a prompt fence and a section break. Harm: the reader has to hunt for what is being judged, at the one beat whose whole job is a comparison. Candidates in reach are the close-out note, the ticket, and the five rules.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Name the noun: 'Does the close-out sound like the comments already on the ticket?'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The `**What happened:**` block is OPTIONAL — default is to omit it
rules_evaluated.evidence: 62:'Two things came out of one ticket: a close-out note on the bug you shipped, and the conventions your team has been encoding in its fields all along.' Three moves present: count plus noun ('Two things'), one qualifier on what makes them the reader's ('your team has been encoding'), and the destination at 64 ('The field rules stay in the scrollback. The next exercise sweeps this whole session.'). Past tense on the narration, present tense on the still-true state, per the tense clause. 44 words across 62-64, slightly over the 25-40 band and the closest thing to a violation here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest line: 39:'Push back on the five.' — 'push back' is the house peer-flat verb for steering, not one of the rule's combative list (bark/order/command/whip/force/drag/boss). Every other human-to-agent verb in the body is 'ask' (33, 45, 58) or 'tell' (53).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: 55:'## Anything can be reverse-engineered' — a header whose literal reading is the very overreach §12 is filed on above. It survives §18 because the section's actual claim IS that generalisation (57), so the header does not contradict its own mechanism; the missing boundary is a §12 fault, not a naming one. 'Other X' shape absent throughout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest to (a) empty negation: 29:'One ticket gives a sample of your team's rules, not the policy.' — this negates against a prior the reader really holds (one ticket reads as the rule), so it earns the contrast. No deictic drumroll, no bold-label echo (widget chrome only), no citation duplication.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: 33:'propose five bug rules' and 39:'Push back on the five.' The five are what the agent will produce at runtime, not items enumerated in an adjacent body list, so the numeral is a handle the reader carries into the next beat rather than a tally of visible bullets. 62's 'Two things' names two items in the same sentence and is the shape §16 prescribes.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 57:'Anything can be inspected and reverse-engineered with an LLM' carries the superlative tell, and the truth test is close: a third-party binary or a SaaS you have no access to is a counterexample. It stays inside because the claim is about what the move affords rather than a bare 'only/always', and the maintainer's stance at 132-134 records 'contested: the reach of anything' as a deliberate choice with a downstream boundary. The defect is that the boundary is missing, which is §12's remedy failing, not §21's no-true-reading case — so it is filed there and not doubled here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A sentence saying how you'd know points at the outcome, not the nearest artifact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 53:'Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket?' points the test at an external artifact the student did not write — the comments already on the ticket — which can come back negative. That is the passing shape; a self-witnessing version would have asked whether the close-out reads well.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session / task / run split (all trainings).
rules_evaluated.evidence: 5:'This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.' Noun-'run' for the agent's sitting is banned in student-facing body; the sanctioned nouns are session (what opens fresh) and task (what lands). Harm: the corpus teaches one-session-one-task through its own vocabulary, and a stray noun-run at line 5 of an M1 exercise unteaches it on the first page. Not one of the survivals — this is not a CI/test/eval execution, not a quoted string, not a path or branch name, not the 'long-running' adjective.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: 'the session' or 'the work' — and the line owes a §1 fix on the same pass.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: 43:'Adding a connector is one command per tracker.' — 'connector' arrives cold. It stays inside on the audience-tier carve-out, and the file's maintainer block at 72 records the ruling explicitly ('engineer audience knows MCP/connectors; the term owes no one-breath earning'), with instruction not to re-file. Every other term in the body ('tracker', 'repro steps', 'close-out', 'LLM') is ordinary engineer vocabulary rather than a house coinage.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — THIS RULE HAS AN EXCEPTION; read to the boundary before cutting anything.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: 18:'If there is no ticket for this bug, say so in the chat. The agent will offer to create one.' and 30:'No ticket of your own to read? Any other real ticket from your tracker works.' Both are plausible-failure plus non-obvious-rescue, one tight line each, next to the risk — the boundary clause keeps them in body, and routing them below the fence would delete them.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 53 is the register beat this rule's own commentary names as sitting inside its exemption (reading for register is allowed where error-catching is not). Per that same clause I re-ran the other axes rather than stopping: actor and mechanism are named ('tell Claude which line and how you'd write it'), the speech verb has an explicit addressee ('tell Claude', not a bare 'say'), and the tell is stated. The one thing missing is the OBJECT — 'it' is never named — and that is filed under check_writing §15 rather than doubled here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran awk 'NR<66 && /—/{print NR": "$0}' over the raw source — no output, zero em-dashes in the body region. Longest body sentence is 57 at 42 words; it is a colon-plus-list, which the rule's read-aloud test survives.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 43: link text is 'MCP and connectors', the target's H1 title, not a filename and not a backticked path — which is what this rule governs. The '../trainings/...' depth-counted prefix in the same link is a path-form question this rule explicitly disclaims (path form belongs to curriculum/module-shape.md § Cross-doc links); noted for the maintainer rather than filed here. No ordinal cross-references anywhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The split is held deliberately: acting takes 'the agent' (18, 29, 30, 31, 58), addressee takes 'Claude' (33, 45, 53), and the one capability-about-thinking claim takes 'LLM' (57). Body counts are agent 6 / Claude 3, the opposite of the assistant-shaped 10:0 audit signal. Backing note at 125 records the same split as a deliberate reshape.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No time-of-day anchors in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: 11:'at the start of every session' — session-relative, which is the sanctioned replacement shape, not a time-of-day anchor. No tomorrow/overnight/this morning/tonight/yesterday anywhere in lines 1-65.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: 37:'There is no penalty if you skip this, and it is completely fine either way.' — true, and it changes nothing the student does. It is filed under check_writing §9, whose flag list names 'no penalty' verbatim and which is the more specific home; double-filing would credit two rules for one line. Nothing else in the body reads as implementation detail before point of use: 43's connector pointer is one clause and 32's outcome-not-recipe test passes on it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 24:'At this point the student should notice the test is still red.' sits directly after a prompt fence and tells the reader to notice something — the rule's exact shape. It is filed under check_writing §7 instead, because the dominant fault is the third-person teacher voice and because the sentence's deeper problem is that the thing to be noticed is not on screen at all (see notes); calling it dead weight would understate it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: 64:'The next exercise sweeps this whole session.' — subject is a later beat, which normally reads as cartography. It stays because check_writing §16 move 3 requires the recap to land on the destination or on what reads the artifact next, and this is that sentence in its prescribed form. Apply the deletion test and 64's first half is left dangling ('The field rules stay in the scrollback.' with nothing picking them up), so it is not NVA.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Length scales with the PROMPT's length, not a fixed ceiling — default short (2026-08-12).
rules_evaluated.evidence: 20:'Drop the ticket link after the colon.' — this is the sub-case with the mechanical trigger: the close-the-ticket-1 fence ends on a dangling 'Ticket:' (verified in the expanded view), and the lead-in is exactly the input instruction with no summary bolted in front of it. Closest to failing is 45:'Ask Claude to write the close-out, update the ticket, and report what it wrote.' over a three-sentence fence — it enumerates all three clauses, which is the tell, but the fence is multi-step enough to carry a fuller cue.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 33:'Ask Claude to reverse-engineer how your team handles bugs and propose five bug rules.' rhymes exactly with the fence's opening 'Reverse-engineer how this team handles bugs from one bug ticket.' Weakest pair is 45 vs the third fence, which opens 'Update the ticket:' while the lead-in leads on 'write the close-out' — same nouns, verbs in swapped order; a rhyme rather than a break.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Tell me what you wrote, not show me what you'll write.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The close-the-ticket-3 fence, expanded, ends 'Tell me what you wrote.' on a side-effecting action (updating a real ticket) — the rule's prescribed default rather than a pre-confirm. The action is correctable after the fact, so the irreversible/external-trust carve-out does not apply and post-action report is right.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompts live in registry; module/exercise/lecture files reference by marker.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 22, 35, 47 carry bare '{{prompt:close-the-ticket-N}}' markers on their own lines, each preceded by a lead-in sentence — the registry shape, no inline fences in the file at all (fence_ranges is empty in the derived view).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named.
rules_evaluated.evidence: AE101 M1's target is earned-trust/curious-readiness, and the body leaves the reader holding two artifacts and a generalisation (62, 57) rather than a resolved doubt. Closest to a mood defect is 11's ritual sentence, which reaches for habit-formation warmth the beat has not earned; scored under check_writing §2.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Whole-compendium scope call: check_sales_copy does not apply to this surface.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The file is a student-facing AE101 exercise body, not site, newsletter, sponsor-deck or pricing copy; no headline, CTA, phase title or ownership claim exists to judge. The two rules with cross-surface reach (§9 em-dashes, §5 M-number cross-references) are clean anyway: zero em-dashes in body, and no bare M-number appears in lines 1-65.

findings.quote: This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.
findings.harm: Banned word 'crucially' in student-facing body — consultancy register the hook normally rewrites, shipped here on the first page an AE101 engineer reads.
findings.fix: Drop the adverb: 'This is the step that changes how the session behaves.'

findings.harm: Noun-'run' for the agent's sitting, banned in student-facing body; it contradicts the one-session-one-task vocabulary the training teaches.

findings.quote: Treat this as a ritual you repeat at the start of every session.
findings.harm: Hard-banned word. Frames the loop as ceremony — the Scrum-retro register this curriculum exists to replace.
findings.fix: Cut, or 'This is an exercise you repeat at the start of every session.'

findings.quote: At this point the student should notice the test is still red.
findings.harm: Third-person teacher voice in body: the reader is described rather than addressed, and a delivery-mechanics observation sits above the fence. It also asserts a state that is false here — this exercise runs after fix-tests-first, where the PR is already shipped.

findings.quote: This section previously said something different; it was fixed on 2026-01-14.
findings.harm: Session biography in student-facing body: a transition verb plus a date, telling the reader about an edit instead of stating what is true. Rules are rules; history is git.

findings.quote: There is no penalty if you skip this, and it is completely fine either way.
findings.harm: Over-hedge. 'No penalty' is on the flag list verbatim, and the second clause repeats the first; a senior engineer reads it and asks why the author is defending the option.
findings.fix: Cut. The push-back paragraph at 39 already invites the skip without apologising for it.

findings.quote: Anything can be inspected and reverse-engineered with an LLM
findings.harm: The slogan ships with no boundary paragraph downstream — the section has only two bullets. The backing stance at line 134 asserts the caveat lives in 'the third bullet', which does not exist, so the next judge is told not to flag a carve-out that was never there. Pre-existing: the same two-bullet section stands in curriculum/exercises/close-the-ticket.md.
findings.fix: Restore the boundary bullet (extraction quality tracks the quality of what was sampled), or strike the third-bullet clause from the stance. Do not hedge line 57.

findings.quote: Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket?
findings.harm: Dangling pronoun at a section opener: 'it' has no antecedent inside '## Double-check the voice', and the close-out note it means was last named at 45, across a prompt fence. The one beat whose job is a comparison never names what is being compared.
findings.fix: 'Does the close-out sound like the comments already on the ticket?'

todos.note: Cut the no-penalty reassurance; structural framing already carries the optionality.
Missing boundary bullet under the anything-can-be-reverse-engineered slogan; backing stance at 134 claims a third bullet that does not exist. Pre-existing in the live exercise.
Name the close-out instead of 'it' at the Double-check the voice opener.
Noun-run to session on the same pass as the §1 banned-word fix.

notes: Body region 1-65, maintainer cut at 66, fence_ranges empty (all prompts are registry markers; read the expanded view for fence content since has_prompt_blocks was true). Brief built cleanly: 129 rules across check_writing, check_student_facing, check_prompts, check_sales_copy, check_strategy_tie_in, 0 dropped, so no compendium was read from an index. Per the dispatch instruction for this run I emitted rows only for rules with something to say, not a full N/A ledger. Two items belong to sibling classes, recorded here rather than in rules_evaluated: (1) TECHNICAL/cross_module — line 24 asserts 'the test is still red', but the maintainer block at 70 places this exercise after fix-tests-first with the PR already shipped, so the claimed state contradicts the arc; deleting the line per check_writing §7 resolves both. (2) PATH FORM — line 43's link uses a depth-counted '../trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/...' prefix, which curriculum/module-shape.md § Cross-doc links forbids in source; check_student_facing §18 governs link TEXT only and explicitly disclaims path form, so it is not filed as a writing finding.
